title: Hand off spreadsheet (CSV) totals and cleanup

steps.title: What we'll do today
steps.html:
From here on it's real work: handing everyday tasks to Claude. First up: spreadsheet cleanup.

Today you'll take a branch sales file, find odd data, make a clean copy and add up the totals.

What's a CSV?

A spreadsheet saved as a text file with commas (,) between the cells. It opens in Excel and in Notepad. It's the easiest table format for Claude to read and edit, so we'll use CSV today.

  • Time: 20 minutes
  • You need: a computer that finished the desktop basics. No Excel needed

steps.title: Download the sample sales file
steps.html:
18 rows of November coffee sales from three branches (Gangnam, Hongdae, Busan). A few mistakes are hidden in it on purpose, and you'll find them with Claude today.

⬇ Download the sample sales.csv

It's saved as sales.csv in your computer's Downloads folder.

steps.title: If the download doesn't work
steps.html:
• If clicking shows text on the screen instead, save it there with Ctrl+S (⌘+S on a Mac) as sales.csv.
  • If you're on a phone, open this page on your computer.

steps.title: Move it into the Practice folder
steps.html:
Claude only works on files in the folder you chose (Practice), so the download needs to go there.

  1. Open File Explorer (Finder on a Mac) and click Downloads on the left.
  2. Also open the Practice folder on your desktop. Put the two windows side by side.
  3. Drag sales.csv into the Practice window.
steps.alt: Dragging sales.csv from the Downloads window into the Practice window

check.q: Is sales.csv in the Practice folder?

steps.title: If dragging is tricky
steps.html:
1. In Downloads, right-click sales.csv and choose Cut (Copy on a Mac).
  2. Right-click an empty spot in the Practice folder and choose Paste.

steps.title: Start with a new chat
steps.html: Claude app → Code tab → + New. Check the buttons under the typing box show Local · Practice · Manual.

check.q: Can you see Local · Practice · Manual?

steps.title: If the start screen looks different
steps.html:
• If the folder isn't Practice, click the folder button → Open folder… and choose it.
  • Click the permission mode button and choose Manual.

steps.title: First ask what the data is
steps.html: With a new file, start by asking what's in it. It's only reading, so it won't ask permission.
steps.code: Explain simply what kind of data sales.csv has

check.q: Did it explain columns like date, branch, item, qty, unit price and amount?

steps.title: If it can't find the file
steps.html:
• Check sales.csv is inside the Practice folder. Claude can't see it in Downloads.
  • Check the folder under the typing box is Practice.

steps.title: Have it find odd data
steps.html: Don't have it fix things right away. Have it find them first. It's safer to fix things once you know what's wrong.
steps.alt: Claude finds a misspelled branch, a duplicate row and a blank quantity
steps.code: Find anything odd in sales.csv. Don't fix it yet

check.q: Did it find problems like the branch name, a duplicate and a blank?

steps.title: If it found something different or tries to fix it
steps.html:
• Three problems are hidden: "Gang nam", a duplicate Nov 8 Gangnam Americano row, and a blank Qty for Busan Cake on Nov 10. If it missed some, say "Look once more for anything else."
  • If a permission card appears, Deny it. It's not time to fix yet.

steps.title: Keep the original; make a clean copy
steps.html:
Don't fix the original directly. Have it make a new file, so the original survives if anything goes wrong. (The copy habit from Desktop 6!)

Read the create-file permission card and click Allow.
steps.code: Leave the original as is and make a new file, sales_clean.csv, with those problems fixed. Fill the blank Qty with Amount ÷ UnitPrice, and save it so Excel opens it correctly

check.q: Is there a new sales_clean.csv in the Practice folder?

steps.title: If the clean copy wasn't made
steps.html:
• If you denied the card, send it again and allow it.
  • If the card edits the original (sales.csv), deny it and say "Don't touch the original; make a new file."

steps.title: Add up totals by branch
steps.html: Now calculate from the clean copy. Always say which file to use.
steps.alt: A table of total sales by branch from the cleaned file
steps.code: Using sales_clean.csv, show total sales by branch, largest first, as a table

check.q: Did you get Gangnam 277.00 · Hongdae 266.50 · Busan 153.00?

steps.title: If the numbers differ
steps.html:
• If Gangnam shows 340.00, the duplicate row is still in. If Gangnam is 251.00 with a separate "Gang nam" of 26.00, the names weren't merged.
  • Say "Check sales_clean.csv again, fix the duplicate and 'Gang nam', then recalculate."
  • Checking against numbers you know is the most important habit at work.

steps.title: Open it in Excel to check
steps.html:
Double-click sales_clean.csv in the Practice folder. If you have Excel, it opens there.

  • Check it has 17 rows (one duplicate removed), "Gang nam" became "Gangnam", and the Nov 10 Busan Cake Qty is filled in as 2.
  • No Excel? Notepad (TextEdit on a Mac) works too.

check.q: Can you see the cleaned data?

steps.title: If Excel shows garbled text
steps.html:
Excel sometimes misreads text in CSV files. Close Excel and tell Claude:

"sales_clean.csv looks garbled in Excel. Save it again as UTF-8 with BOM."

Allow the card, then open it again.

steps.title: Try asking for these too
steps.html:
• "How many of each item were sold, as a table"
  • "Sort by date and save as sales_sorted.csv"
  • "What's the best-selling item at each branch?"
  • "Which branch has the highest average daily sales?"
With your real files, put a copy in the Practice folder first. Be careful with files containing personal data like customer names or phone numbers.

steps.title: 🎉 Work practice 1 done! What you learned
steps.html:
Finding and adding things up one by one in Excel took just a few sentences.

Ask what it is→Find problems first→Make a separate clean copy→Calculate and check

Three rules for real work

  1. Have it find problems before fixing. Know what's wrong first.
  2. Keep the original; make a new file. You can always go back.
  3. Check the numbers. Comparing against one total you know prevents big mistakes.
